Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery is a Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) cemetery located in the Somme department of northern France. Here's what I know about it:

## Location and Setting
- Located near the village of Beaumont-Hamel, about 10 km north of Albert
- Part of the Somme battlefield area
- Situated within or near the Beaumont-Hamel Newfoundland Memorial Park

## Historical Context
- Connected to the Battle of the Somme (1916), particularly the first day on July 1, 1916
- Beaumont-Hamel was one of the objectives for British forces on that catastrophic first day
- The area saw some of the heaviest casualties, particularly for the Newfoundland Regiment

## The Cemetery
- Contains graves of soldiers who fell during the Battle of the Somme and subsequent fighting
- Like most CWGC cemeteries, it features uniform white headstones and is meticulously maintained
- May include both identified and unidentified burials

## Significance
- Part of the larger memorial landscape of the Somme
- Near the preserved battlefield and trench systems at Beaumont-Hamel
- The area is particularly significant to Newfoundlanders due to the devastating losses suffered by the Newfoundland Regiment on July 1, 1916

## Visiting
- Open to the public year-round
- Part of the Somme battlefield tour route
- Often visited in conjunction with the Newfoundland Memorial Park

The cemetery serves as a permanent memorial to those who fell in one of the First World War's most intense and costly battles.
